name: Mara des Bois
classification_notes: Capitals drawn from David Lance Goines' 1970s-80s Chez Panisse lettering give it inscriptional Roman proportions and Art Nouveau gestures, placing it as a display serif rather than a text face.
summary: A display serif built from David Lance Goines' Chez Panisse lettering, with Art Nouveau gestures and triangular serifs.
description: Mara des Bois takes its capitals from lettering David Lance Goines created for Chez Panisse in the 1970s and 80s, a style with inscriptional Roman proportions and linocut warmth. Still in progress on Future Fonts, it is growing into an eight-weight variable family with tabular numbers.
foundry_blurb: Graham Bradley describes Mara des Bois as starting from missing Berkeley: an evening spent drawing capitals based on David Lance Goines' Chez Panisse lettering, a style he'd long admired for its inscriptional proportions, Art Nouveau gestures, triangular serifs and linocut warmth.

name: Madtown
classification_notes: An all-caps display face built from wedge-serifed American West signage letterforms that turn boxy and triangular when condensed.
summary: An all-caps display face drawing on American West signage, with wedge-shaped serifs that turn boxy and triangular when condensed.
description: Madtown takes its cue from wedge-serifed O's found on American West signage, the kind of nineteenth-century letterforms that turn into straight lines and triangles under condensation. Still in progress on Future Fonts, it is currently a single all-caps style with broad European language support.
foundry_blurb: A+ describe Madtown as inspired by letters from the American West, particularly styles with an O carrying wedge-shaped serifs, letterforms that become straight lines, boxy curves and triangles when condensed yet feel clean and contemporary despite their nineteenth-century origins.
